terrain: latency- and quota-sensitive interactive coding with on-demand local extension

levels.0: No qualifying pinned source evidence in this audit.
levels.0.5: A reachable, tested mechanism covers part of the question, but defaultness, completeness or the decisive failure case remains open.
levels.1: The pinned shipped path and executable invariant satisfy the full-pass rule.

questions.prompt: Does the default execution path minimize serial provider hops and blocking secondary work?
questions.full_pass: A shipped default path plus executable invariant isolates the avoided blocking work.

questions.prompt: Does it control context growth or cache reuse with explicit token and invalidation semantics?
questions.full_pass: A shipped path and invariant enforce a token/cache policy rather than only reporting usage.

questions.prompt: Can independent work overlap without losing limits or deterministic model-visible ordering?
questions.full_pass: An executable invariant covers concurrent execution, bounds and deterministic result handling.

questions.prompt: Are resource limits compiled into pre-call, stop or overflow policy?
questions.full_pass: The reachable path enforces a limit before or during execution and tests the boundary.

questions.prompt: Are provider/model-specific reasoning, tool, media and error semantics preserved?
questions.full_pass: Provider-specific translation is reachable and executable tests cover non-common-denominator semantics.

questions.prompt: Are external tools and protocols supported through a tested lifecycle rather than bespoke core patches?
questions.full_pass: A shipped protocol/tool lifecycle has discovery, invocation and failure invariants.

questions.prompt: Can capability changes become usable without privileged core edits or process restart?
questions.full_pass: Executable tests cover load or refresh, use and cleanup/rollback on the live path.

questions.prompt: Do translation and extension failures remain typed, attributable and recoverable?
questions.full_pass: The shipped boundary preserves actionable failure semantics and tests recovery or isolation.

questions.prompt: Is decisive task state durably persisted rather than held only in process memory?
questions.full_pass: The shipped session path persists enough ordered state to reconstruct useful work.

questions.prompt: Does persistence remain coherent across torn writes, interruption or partial failure?
questions.full_pass: An executable failure invariant covers atomicity, repair, idempotency or a durable transaction.

questions.prompt: Can interrupted work resume without losing decisive state or blindly repeating effects?
questions.full_pass: Recovery/replay tests classify interruption and reconstruct a safe next state.

questions.prompt: Can users reverse or branch work without mutating the source state?
questions.full_pass: Executable tests cover non-destructive revert, undo or fork semantics.

anti_overfit_rules: The exam file contains no candidate names or candidate-specific weights.
Question text, weights and level anchors are shared by every candidate.
Missing evidence scores zero; popularity, testimonials and feature count score nothing.
Results live in a separate answer file and cannot redefine the exam.
Runtime outcomes remain a separate promotion stage and may overturn this source order.
